label: Degenerate Configurations
notes: Open by reframing degeneracy as geometric non-uniqueness rather than measurement noise. A critical configuration leaves a whole alternative camera or reconstruction model consistent with the same images, so estimation has no preferred answer. We will diagnose each case through rank, nullspace, surface incidence, or homography fit across this chapter.

label: What Degeneracy Means
notes: Stress the distinction between a noisy estimate and a degenerate one. With noise a unique model exists but is perturbed; with degeneracy a one-parameter or larger family of models fits the data exactly. The remedy is not better optimisation but detecting the condition and routing to a smaller, well-posed model.

label: Planar Scenes Fail to Fix F
notes: Explain the most common practical degeneracy: all points on a plane. One plane-induced homography transfers every correspondence, so the fundamental matrix is undetermined. Point at the singular-value tail of the eight-point design matrix, where extra nullity appears, contrasting the clean rank-eight spatial case against the rank-deficient planar one.

label: Homography Explains the Data
notes: Make the algebra explicit. When points lie on a plane the correspondences satisfy x' equals H x, and any F of the form skew-e times H solves the epipolar constraint, giving a pencil of valid fundamental matrices. The epipole is free, so the second camera is not recovered. This motivates the homography-versus-F decision.

label: Pure Rotation
notes: Cover the second motion degeneracy: zero baseline. With a fixed camera centre the images differ only by the calibration-conjugated rotation homography, and there is no parallax to triangulate. The essential matrix collapses because the translation is null. A spatial, non-planar cloud still degenerates, showing the cause is motion, not scene shape.

label: Critical Surfaces and the Horopter
notes: Introduce the two-view critical surface theorem: ambiguity arises when both camera centres and all scene points lie on a ruled quadric. The horopter, a twisted cubic through both centres, is the locus of points imaged identically. Emphasise that incidence with this quadric is the hidden geometric reason behind the ambiguity, not coincidence.

label: The Ruled Quadric Visualised
notes: Walk through the doubly ruled quadric z equals xy. Fixing x gives one family of straight generators, fixing y gives the other; both camera centres and the points sit exactly on the surface. The conjugate reconstruction slides points along generators, so structure and motion are recoverable only up to this quadric family.

label: Resectioning Degeneracy
notes: Turn to single-camera resection. Ambiguity is organised by the pencil P-theta equals P plus theta P-alt. When the pencil keeps rank three the nullspace is a single centre; when rank drops the nullspace becomes a line or plane joining the critical set. The classical case is the centre with points on a twisted cubic through it.

label: Rank Drop in the Pencil
notes: Read the numerical proof. As theta sweeps, the smallest singular value of P-theta dips to zero at the exceptional value where the shared block cancels; rank falls from three to one and nullity rises to three. That dimension jump is exactly the linear component the chapter adds to the resection critical set.

label: Carlsson-Weinshall Duality
notes: Sketch the duality map Gamma sending each homogeneous coordinate to the product of the other three. Away from coordinate planes it acts like reciprocation, exchanging points and cameras. The lesson is that a simple line statement about points and centres dualises into a twisted-cubic statement, unifying resection and reconstruction degeneracies under one map.

label: Detecting Degeneracy: H vs F
notes: Bring in model selection. RANSAC alone can fit a confident but meaningless F on planar or rotational data, so compare a homography against the fundamental matrix on the same matches. GRIC scores each model with a penalty for parameters and structure dimension, selecting H when the plane explanation wins and avoiding a spurious projective reconstruction.

label: Diagnostic Scorecard
notes: Close with a preflight checklist an implementation should run before trusting a reconstruction: eight-point nullity, planarity ratio, baseline length, homography transfer versus Sampson error, and three-view quadric dependence. The aim is not to reject planar or rotational data but to route each sequence to the correctly posed model.

label: Summary
notes: Recap the unifying thread: degeneracy is non-uniqueness diagnosed through rank, nullspace, and surface incidence. Planar scenes and pure rotation are homography-dominated; two-view ambiguity lives on a ruled quadric and horopter; resection critical sets are rank drops in a camera pencil; and model selection separates the cases in practice.
